 Political Watch: November 19, 2026 
 by 
 Caleb Wiseblood 
 November 19, 2026 November 18, 2026

 • In response to proposed Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) cuts that could impact approximately 6 million citizens, U.S. Rep. Salud Carbajal (D-Santa Barbara) issued a statement on Nov. 10. “Over the past year, I visited food banks across the Central Coast and saw firsthand how the initial round of SNAP cuts put a big strain on seniors, veterans, children, and more,” Carbajal stated, referring to program cuts enacted in July 2025. “It is just heartless to do this again to families who are already struggling under the Trump administration’s failed economic policies. … I’m outraged that the Trump administration is proposing an additional round of deep SNAP cuts that could hurt millions of families nationwide, … including over 300,000 people in California.” According to Carbajal’s office, the proposed revision would cut federal spending on SNAP benefits by $44.65 billion over the course of five years (fiscal years 2027 through 2031), while simultaneously increasing California state spending on SNAP administrative expenses by $928.5 million. In his role as a member of the House Agriculture Committee, Carbajal stated that he “will continue to fight for Central Coast families and work to roll back these terrible cuts.”
 • On Nov. 13, Allan Hancock College Superintendent and President Kevin G. Walthers issued a statement about Measure H securing enough votes, more than 55 percent, to pass. This voter-approved ballot measure authorizes up to $290 million in “locally controlled general obligation bonds to build, upgrade, and modernize facilities at the college,” according to a release from Hancock. “This funding represents a tremendous responsibility, and we will work to ensure every dollar is spent responsibly and transparently on projects that strengthen our facilities, support student success, and serve our communities for generations to come,” Walthers stated. “We are deeply grateful to our community for its continued investment in Hancock and, most importantly, in the students we serve.” According to Hancock, the projects expected to receive priority consideration for Measure H bond funding include developing a University Center, improving facilities that support Hancock’s nursing and healthcare education programs, and critical repairs and upgrades to campus infrastructure. “This is an important moment for the future of Hancock,” Hancock board President Suzanne Levy stated in the Nov. 13 release. “The board of trustees looks forward to working with college leadership to carefully prioritize projects that address our most pressing needs, expand educational opportunities, and ensure Hancock remains a place where future generations can learn, grow and succeed.”
 • On Nov. 12, U.S. Sens. Alex Padilla (D-California), Richard Blumenthal (D-Connecticut), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts) co-introduced the End Veterans Homelessness Act to help address the veteran housing crisis in California and across the country . This legislation would expand veterans’ eligibility for housing vouchers through the Department of Housing and Urban Development-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH) program while reducing casework bottlenecks that prevent veterans from securing housing. As of July 2026, Congress has funded nearly 116,000 HUD-VASH vouchers, but about 20,900 of these vouchers are not being used in part due to strict statutory requirements, according to Padilla’s office. “Too many federally funded HUD-VASH vouchers are going unused every year due to red tape and outdated eligibility requirements,” Padilla stated. Specifically, the End Veterans Homelessness Act would broaden HUD-VASH eligibility to include veterans and their families who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness and veterans who do not require intensive supportive services (and are currently ineligible for the program), while preserving priority for chronically homeless veterans and veterans with chronic disabilities.
 This article appears in November 19 – November 26, 2026 .
